summary: Monaco's government says foreign nationals staying under three months need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France. Nationals of the European Economic Area and associated states need no visa, only a valid passport or identity card; nationals of other countries need a valid passport and a Schengen entry visa, applied for at the embassy of the Schengen country through which they enter Europe, though for stays under 90 days certain nationalities are exempt from the Schengen visa. The UK government says France handles immigration matters for Monaco and that the Schengen area's 90-day visa-free limit includes Monaco.

tips.text: Monaco's government says foreign nationals staying less than three months must hold the passport, and any visa, required to enter France; nationals of the European Economic Area and associated states need a valid passport or identity card.

The UK government says you can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Monaco, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days.
The UK government says you could get a fine in Monaco if you walk around in swimsuits, stripped to the waist, or barefoot, apart from on beaches and in bathing areas.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Monaco?
faq.answer: Monaco's government says foreign nationals staying under three months need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France. Nationals of the European Economic Area and associated states need no visa, only a valid passport or identity card; for stays under 90 days certain nationalities are exempt from the Schengen visa; others need a Schengen visa from the embassy of the Schengen country that will be their point of entry into Europe, after which Monaco can be visited without any other formality.

faq.question: Is Monaco in the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: The UK government says Monaco follows Schengen area rules, that France handles immigration matters for Monaco, and that the Schengen area includes Monaco. Monaco's government says visitors need the passport, and any visa, required to enter France.

faq.answer: Monaco's government says foreign visitors must hold the passport, and any visa, required to enter France, and that EEA nationals need a valid passport or identity card. No official source we could read says when identity is checked on the way into Monaco.

faq.question: How can I stay in Monaco longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Monaco's government says anyone aged 16 or over who wishes to stay in Monaco for more than three months a year, or to settle there, must apply to the Monegasque authorities for a residence card (carte de séjour). It says you must apply for an establishment visa (type D) for Monaco at the French consulate nearest your last home, and lists proof of sufficient resources among the documents to gather.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Monaco?
faq.answer: The UK government says you can travel without a visa to the Schengen area, which includes Monaco, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days. The United States is listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period.
